title: About the pitfall of erroneous validation data in the estimation of confusion matrices
relevance: States our recurring problem in remote-sensing terms and gives it a direction: when reference errors are CORRELATED with a classifier's errors, accuracy is OVERESTIMATED and that classifier is systematically favoured over its competitors, whereas conditionally independent reference errors cause underestimation. That is exactly finding 5 - the corrected model landed beside the NDVI reference (35% vs 37.7%) rather than C-CAP's (29.5%), and scoring it against that same reference would flatter it by construction. Also proposes a maximum-entropy correction, and concludes that a few HIGH-QUALITY trusted labels beat a larger volume of questionable reference data - a direct steer for the P3 sample design.

authors: Persson, H.J., Ekstrom, M. & Stahl, G.
title: Quantify and account for field reference errors in forest remote sensing studies
relevance: Forest-specific treatment of reference error as a quantity to be MEASURED and propagated rather than assumed away, with estimators that carry it through to the final figures. Relevant because every number we publish is scored against a proxy whose own error we have never quantified, and STATE's standing caveat ('both refs are PROXIES') is currently a sentence rather than a term in an equation. Gives the machinery to turn that caveat into an error budget with a number attached, which is what the deliverable needs if the per-crown intervals are to mean anything.
